test_title: PYST 24: RRB Group D - Mathematics (Held On: 08 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Pipes A and B can fill 50% of a tank in 15 and 10 minutes, respectively. There is also an emptying pipe C attached to the tank. If all the three pipes are opened together, the tank is filled in 15 minutes. If the tank is two-third filled, then in how much time (in minutes) C alone will empty the tank completely?
solution:
**Given:**

A fills 50% in 15 min

B fills 50% in 10 min

A + B + C fills full tank in 15 min

Required work = 2/3 tank

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Work ÷ Time

Net efficiency = Sum of filling − emptying

Time = Work ÷ Efficiency

**Calculation:**

⇒ A fills full tank in 30 min

⇒ B fills full tank in 20 min

⇒ LCM of 30, 20, 15 = 60

⇒ Work done by A in 1 min = 60 ÷ 30 = 2

⇒ Work done by B in 1 min = 60 ÷ 20 = 3

⇒ Work done by (A + B + C) in 1 min = 60 ÷ 15 = 4

⇒ Work done by C in 1 min = 4 − (2 + 3) = −1

⇒ C empties 1 unit per min

⇒ Total work = 60

⇒ Required work = (2 ÷ 3) × 60 = 40

⇒ Time = 40 ÷ 1 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**
